params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The whole room goes at once. At the far left the small terracotta cube creature writes at furious speed and flings finished pages over its shoulder, one after another, into the air around the towers. The small lavender cloud creature at the foot of the server rack springs up at the screen that hangs out of the rack, drops, and springs up again. At the far right the round grey creature with the pointed ears hoists the sledgehammer high and whips it down onto the rubble again and again, chips flying. In the near right the small blue-purple star creature whirls into a spinning smear, arms flung out, sketches flying from its hands, stops dead, and whirls again. In the middle of it all, far away at the desk on the far wall, the young man spins his chair round on the spot in one fast turn to face us, his back to the monitors now, both hands gripping the armrests, and his head turns from the far left of the room to the far right, taking it all in, his eyes wide and his mouth open in dismay, and holds there, facing us from his desk.

Each character stays on its own spot in every frame and lands on the floor after every leap. The cube creature keeps exactly one pencil in every frame. The cloud creature keeps its pale chevron-and-bar face in every frame. The grey creature keeps its two eyes, its wide grin and its two pointed ears in every frame. The star keeps its five points and stays the same size and on the same spot in every frame. The young man stays in his chair at the desk in every frame, and the chair stays on the same spot on the floor in front of the desk in every frame — it turns on the spot and goes nowhere. He stays the same small, far-away size in every frame, the top of his head below the cork board on the wall behind him in every frame. His short blonde hair, his stubble and his navy T-shirt are the same in every frame, and from the moment he faces us his face is the same face in every frame. The camera stays exactly where it is; nothing comes closer to the camera. The room stays the same drawing in every frame: the towers of paper, the server rack and its screen, the doorway, the desk and monitors, the hole and the rocket, the television, the dartboard, the paper on the floor.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
